title: sse: add per-event sequence tag and tolerant reassembly to recover from framing skew
author: Asha Patel
description: Context: We occasionally see production reassembly failures for OpenAI-compat SSE streams when intermediate proxies or middleware mutate whitespace/delimiters (trim, collapse) or when client-side transport reorders fragments during retry. Symptoms were: partial JSON payloads after stream end, duplicate function_call sentinels, and occasional 'unexpected token' errors during structured JSON reconstruction. These failures were often transient but impactful to callers relying on streaming structured outputs and tool/function-call boundaries. Motivation: previous fixes focused on strict 'data:' marker parsing and delimiter normalization. That approach is brittle when components in the path remove empty 'data:' lines or coalesce adjacent events. This PR makes the reassembler resilient by (1) adding an optional per-event monotonic sequence tag (sseq) that travels with each SSE event, (2) tolerating missing separators by using sseq ordering to reorder/hold events, and (3) hardening sentinel handling for function/tool calls so overlapping fragments do not generate duplicated function_call events. Design summary: - New event header: 'sseq: <uint64>' (opaque to clients if not used) appended to SSE payloads emitted by the OpenAI compatibility layer. It's optional and backward-compatible: receivers without support ignore it. - Reassembler changes: keep a small out-of-order buffer (configurable window) keyed by sseq; if sseq is present, reorder within window and attempt merge; if sseq missing, fall back to existing time-based heuristic but mark stream as 'skew-suspect'. - Trimming safety: avoid aggressive whitespace stripping on event boundaries; only trim inside the JSON body where safe. - Function-call sentinel fix: canonicalize the function_call sentinel into a single atomic token and ensure it is emitted only when the reassembler has seen a full sentinel (prevents duplication when sentinel splits across fragments). Backwards compatibility & deployment: - The new header is enabled by default on server side but will be omitted for legacy clients unless feature-negotiation indicates support. - A rollout flag (OPENAI_COMPAT_SSE_SEQ=false) is available for hot rollback. - Added migration notes and docs for partners (proxy/nginx recommendations). Tests & validation: - Unit tests for reassembly state machine covering small/medium/large fragment windows. - Integration e2e harness that simulates common proxy mutations: trimming, concatenation, delayed reordering. - Live-canary on dedicated region for 24h before full rollout. Checklist: - [x] Add sseq header emission in compat layer - [x] Implement reassembly buffer and ordering logic - [x] Add trimming-safety heuristics - [x] Harden function_call sentinel detection - [x] Unit + integration tests - [x] Canary and monitoring dashboards added - [x] Docs and rollout notes included How to reproduce locally: 1) run the sse reassembly e2e in packages/harness with the `--mutate-proxy` flag. 2) run a client that expects structured function_call across stream boundary; both the old and new reassemblers are exercised by toggling OPENAI_COMPAT_SSE_SEQ. Notes: - This is targeted at streams that carry structured JSON/function calls and is intentionally permissive to avoid dropping user payloads. If strict delimiter behavior is required for some customers, use the rollout flag to disable reordering. - There is a follow-up ticket (ENG-1805) to add optional cryptographic checksums on long multi-event JSON objects to detect silent corruption.

review_comments: Miguel Rivera: Nice approach, Asha. A couple of concerns: what's the memory behavior of the out-of-order buffer under high-rate streams? We should cap and emit a metric when eviction happens.

Asha Patel: Added cap + eviction metrics (pkg/metrics) and a hard cap configurable by OPENAI_COMPAT_SSE_BUFFER_MAX. Evicted sequences get an 'evicted_sseq' counter and we log reassembly-summary at debug level.
Priya Singh: Please add a regression test that reproduces the duplication bug described in SUP-3221. Also can we add a simple backwards-compat test where sseq is absent?
Asha Patel: Added regression test in parser.test.ts and an absence-of-sseq e2e scenario in proxy_mutation_harness. Tests added and passing locally.
Evan Carter: lgtm after one nit: prefer explicit 'sseq' header name in reassembly docs so partners can implement checks. Also please add a short blurb to the SDK streaming README.
Asha Patel: Added explicit header docs and a README blurb in docs/openai-compat and updated SDK note in the TS SDK quickstart.
release_notes: Improve SSE streaming resiliency: added optional per-event sequence header (sseq) and tolerant reassembly logic to recover from trimmed/merged/ reordered fragments. Hardens function_call sentinel handling to avoid duplicate events. Backward-compatible; rollout flag available.
notes_for_backport: Marked backport-ready to 2025.12.4-stable. Recommend patch backport to dedicated and private deployment images where legacy proxies are common.
